subject: Media Literacy
title: The Psychology of Persuasion
description: Learn The Psychology of Persuasion in one minute.

hook.text: You're three times more likely to believe something if it rhymes. 'If the glove don't fit, you must acquit.'

buildup.text: Propaganda exploits cognitive shortcuts: repetition, social proof, authority, and emotional arousal.

discovery.text: The 'illusory truth effect' means we believe things simply because we've heard them before.

twist.text: Even knowing about these biases doesn't make you immune. Awareness helps, but it's not a shield.

climax.text: Propagandists don't need you to believe. They just need you to doubt everything else.

punchline.text: Repeat it enough and the brain stops asking if it's true.

quiz.question: What is the illusory truth effect?
options: Repeated exposure makes statements seem more true
